title: When using the wintab driver, the Y value of the pen tilt is inverted.
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f], v4.8.dev1.official [ebbf577a0]

### System information

Windows 11 (build 26200) - Wacom Intuos Pro PTH-860 (Presumably, other pen tablets that use the wintab driver will also)

### Issue description

When using the wintab driver, the Y value of the pen tilt is inverted.


After examining the Godot Engine code,

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f5af32893ba3774235b5d3c570d8433d079a4b82/platform/windows/display_server_windows.cpp#L5758

I confirmed that the issue can be resolved by reversing the sign of the Y value—either by changing

``` cpp
Math::atan(Math::cos(azim) / alt)
```

to

``` cpp
Math::atan(-Math::cos(azim) / alt)
```

or to

``` cpp
-Math::atan(Math::cos(azim) / alt)
```



However, in this case, when the pen moves out of the hover detection range, the Y value appears to become -0.0 instead of 0.0.
After retrieving the tilt value,

``` cpp
if (tilt.y > -0.0000001 && tilt.y < 0.0000001) {
  tilt.y = std::copysign(tilt.y, 1.0);
}
```

I suppose there is a way to forcibly change the sign as shown above, but I don’t think it’s a very good approach.
Realistically, if leaving it at -0.0 doesn’t cause any problems, it might be better to leave it that way, but I can’t say for sure.


Also, to begin with, while reversing the sign of `Math::atan(Math::cos(azim) / alt)` seems to fix the inversion of the Y-value, I’m not sure if this is the right approach.
Anyway, I’ve written down what I tried.
I’d appreciate it if you could take a look.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect a pen tablet that supports tilt.
2. Import and open `misc > graphics_tablet_input` from [godotengine/godot-demo-projects: Demonstration and Template Projects](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects).
3. Go to Project Settings > Input Devices > Pen Tablet > Driver.windows, set it to "wintab," and restart the Editor.
4. Run the project, and bring the pen close to the pen tablet.
  A red line representing the pen’s tilt will appear, but if you compare it to the pen’s actual tilt, you’ll see that the top and bottom are inverted.
